behavior: Explicit stop/new session clears subscribed/retired sets, bar buffers, quotes, receipt timestamps and aggregate last-update state. Restarted symbols are unseen/stale until valid data arrives; old symbols cannot remain in the freshness universe.
Transport callbacks capture stream identity and generation and admit only current subscribed symbols. Old bar/quote callbacks cannot mutate stopped/restarted sessions, including a reused symbol.

Lifecycle and subscription operations serialize through an asyncio lock. Stop invalidates immediately, before waiting, and again when it acquires the lock; obsolete awaited connect, subscribe, prefill or reconnect continuations cannot reanimate state.
Failed/cancelled start cleans transport and data in finally. A failed disconnect retains its original stream reference until a later cleanup succeeds, while its callbacks and health remain invalid.

Forced same-session recovery preserves stale buffers/receipt ages and revokes the old callback generation. Fresh callbacks are installed only after successful reconnect; reconnect itself never establishes freshness.
limitations: No natural stream/broker or transport-server session was contacted. Tests replace transport only and exercise real provider methods, timestamps and cache state.
Subscription membership remains based on the existing transport boolean/sets contract; this patch does not add server acknowledgement telemetry.

Stop revokes callbacks immediately, then waits for serialized in-flight transport/REST calls to finish so it can disconnect safely. It does not introduce hard cancellation/deadlines beyond existing client behavior.
Retaining same-session stale history on reconnect is intentional; it cannot be mistaken for freshness. Explicit stop/start instead drops all prior-session state.
